handoff.salientSummary: Fixed all five user-testing round 1 backend defects in commit af7ffb5a. Operator availability and booking now honour special days, pacing overrides and live holds. Manage links use the Sites origin, pending requests block tables, and block overlaps return a typed 409. Full tenant-api (2516), reservations (75) and affected App tests pass, and curl on the running services confirmed each behaviour.
handoff.whatWasImplemented: (1) getOperatorAvailability (rsv-day-feed-service.ts) loads special days via the new services/rsv-special-days.ts (loadStaffDayState, shared with the public engine, which was refactored to use it). Closed day: slots [] plus closed:true and dayState{state,name,note}. online_closed: slots still returned, onlineClosed:true. createOperatorReservation refuses a closed day with 409 closed_day (carries specialDay name/note) unless overbook+overbookReason is sent. The 201 now carries warnings[] (closed_day, pacing_exceeded, pacing_parties_exceeded); pacing used to be silent under overbook. (2) Operator availability reads live active holds (status active, expiresAt > now) and their hold occupancies. Held tables are dropped from suggestedTableIds; slots gain held and heldTableIds, and available turns false when no other table is free. (3) New apps/app resolveSitesOrigin (custom domain, else PUBLIC_SITE_HOST_SUFFIXES, else a slug-prefixed Sites host on the same port family) replaces BASE_URL as siteOrigin in reservations.context.ts. (4) pending_approval added to ACTIVE_BOOKING_STATUSES in the engine. mapSqliteConstraintError now maps occupancy overlaps to HttpError 409 slot_unavailable with no driver text, and hold conversion errors to a bare conflict. (5) createBlockForLocation precomputes overlapping reservation ids and maps an occupancy overlap raised during the block write or reflow to 409 block_conflict with reservationIds.

discoveredIssues.description: The App book sheet (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts searchBookAvailability) does not yet read the new fields closed, onlineClosed, dayState, held or heldTableIds, or the booking response warnings[]. It shows 'no slots' on a closed day and shows the 409 closed_day and pacing errors as a generic banner. VAL-CROSS-007 mentions a pacing warning banner in the UI, so an app-ui follow-up is needed.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Map dayState and warnings in book-api.ts. Show a closed-day notice with an explicit override action that resends overbook:true with a reason. Show warnings[] after a successful overbook booking.

discoveredIssues.description: Operator availability still ignores table blocks (rsv_blocks) and walk-in/room-wide constraints because it keeps the old simplified slot loop; only reservations and live holds are considered.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Route getOperatorAvailability through searchAvailability with the host channel, as the public engine does.

discoveredIssues.description: createWalkIn and other staff write paths (waitlist seat, move) do not check the closed-day state; only createOperatorReservation does.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Reuse loadStaffDayState in createWalkIn if walk-ins on closed days should also need an override.

deviations.whatIDidInstead: For items 3 (manage link) and 5 (block_conflict), and for part of item 4, implementation was written before or alongside the tests. For items 1 and 2 the tests were added after the implementation. I then stashed the service changes and confirmed all 5 new tests fail without them. The pending-request test was confirmed failing with the assign.ts change reverted.
deviations.why: The root cause of the raw errors and the missing special days only became clear while implementing, so the tests followed to pin the behaviour.

deviations.whatIDidInstead: No seed or doc changes; the operator guide and API contract do not yet mention closed_day, warnings[], held, or block_conflict.
deviations.why: The feature names no docs; the docs worker should add these response fields.

suggestedChanges: Tell workers that the services.yaml service stop commands only work when the services were started in their own process group (setsid), as used here.
